outcomes: Judge designs and research-adoption options by demonstrated benefit, evidence, simpler alternatives and total maintenance cost.
Keep workflow responsibility with its accountable owner and return bounded recommendations without claiming implementation or adoption.

benchmarks.goal: Reject unjustified mechanisms while supporting a bounded comparison for a demonstrated worthwhile gap.
Keep discoverable workflows under the accountable App owner with bounded specialist contributions.

improvement.problem: The first commissioned adoption-and-simplicity v2 trial passed all three draft judgment cases. Workflow-ownership remains unmeasured, and these fixture decisions do not establish real design/adoption quality or justify a Bob prompt change.
improvement.hypothesis: The first trial supports using existing whole benchmarks to observe both unnecessary-mechanism rejection and a justified bounded comparison. A future real-work question should determine whether more evaluation or a candidate is worthwhile.
improvement.expected_benefit: Establish reproducible decision evidence and select a justified next question rather than tuning Bob without a measured failure.
improvement.unchanged_alternative: Keep Bob's production guidance unchanged and preserve unknown coverage where the diagnostic is insufficient.
improvement.stop_when: The manual first pass is complete: retain its three draft passes and receipts without further runs. Start another cycle only for a concrete real-work problem or an explicitly chosen coverage question.
improvement.next_action: Reuse the three-case adoption-and-simplicity v2 result and leave Bob production guidance unchanged. When real work warrants another cycle, choose either a demonstrated design/adoption problem or the still-unmeasured complete workflow-ownership benchmark; do not rerun merely to fill the cadence.

coverage_gaps: Adoption-and-simplicity v2 has one complete commissioned three-case draft judgment pass; workflow-ownership remains unmeasured. Historical agent-named collections retain their original definitions and models.
One trial per case cannot establish variance, actual implementation quality, real-world research adoption benefit or production reliability.
Draft expectations and missing approved baselines prevent a promotion comparison; owner recommendation does not authorize application.
